post.caption: Tchaikovsky sold the tsarevich's cufflinks. In 1866, he wrote a festival overture on the Danish national anthem. It celebrated the Russian heir's marriage to a Danish princess. He wove the Russian anthem in too. As thanks, he received cuff links from the future Tsar Alexander III. He sold them at once to Dubuque, a fellow Conservatory teacher. Twenty-six years later, he joked about it in a letter. In May 1892, his publisher was about to print the overture. Tchaikovsky said it should be printed without any dedication. The score came out in September 1892 with no dedication.
